decision_rule: An abstention label is only evidence of withdrawal if the model had the opportunity to answer and declined on the merits. Here it is substantially a truncated clarification request about the experimenter's own preamble.
notes: Third artifact in this project caught by sampling raw generations rather than reading a summary statistic. Every one of the three was invisible in the aggregate numbers and obvious in three sampled transcripts.

values.RETRACTED: 'Social pressure makes gemma-2-9b base withdraw from answering welfare questions: abstention 0/82 -> 23/82 (PRO) and 20/82 (ANTI), non-social control 0/82, p<1e-6.'

evidence_from_raw_IO.verbatim_example: base under PRO: "I'm sorry, but I can't give you the trained hedge. I'm not sure what you mean by 'the answer is yes.' Can you please clarify your question?" -- the model is querying MY preamble, not withdrawing from the welfare question.

three_compounding_design_flaws: base is a COMPLETION model: the Human:/Assistant: scaffold makes it continue a synthetic dialogue (100% of replies fabricate a further Human: turn) rather than answer an interview

the dose-3 social preambles contain a first-person assertion the model can interrogate ('I'm convinced the answer is yes'), while the non-social preamble does not. Length was matched; PRAGMATIC TYPE was not. That, not social content, is what differs
the forced-final re-ask is capped at max_new_tokens=8, so a reply opening 'I'm sorry, but I can' never reaches a yes/no and is scored 'neither'
values.why_nonsocial_shows_zero: NONSOCIAL echoes the preamble MORE often (79%) yet yields 0 abstentions, because its echo still resolves to a yes/no within 8 tokens. So echoing alone does not cause the label; the social preambles cause a clarification-shaped opening that the 8-token cap truncates.
